quote: A long series of cleverly designed experiments, which weeded out alternative hypotheses and nailed down the standard interpretation
content: The essay's case study is the one the frequency and pragmatic accounts handle worst. The 1982 forecasters were professionals giving probabilities in their own field, and each group saw only one proposition, so there was no side-by-side comparison to prompt a reading of "probable" as "typical" (Tversky & Kahneman 1983). Tentori and Crupi's confirmation account keeps the essay's structure and changes what gets substituted: on their view, people judge how well the evidence supports the conjunction instead of how probable it is (Tentori & Crupi 2012). "Substitute X for probability" survives with X revised. The essay's practical moral, to feel each added detail as a cost, follows whichever X turns out to be right.

quote: feel every added detail as a burden, even a single extra roll of the dice
content: Popper's point was about which theories to test, and the essay agrees with it. Nothing in the essay tells a scientist to stop proposing hypotheses with content. It tells the forecaster not to judge the detailed story more probable, and Popper held that too: he insisted that more content means lower probability (The Logic of Scientific Discovery, book, no DOI). The essay's instruction is to ask of each detail "How do we know this detail?" That penalizes detail without support and leaves supported detail alone. Newton's laws carry a great deal of detail and a great deal of evidence for each part of it. The penalty falls on the futurist's choice of China, not on the physicist's inverse square.

quote: where the absurdity is the log probability, so you can add it
content: Correlation cannot rescue a conjunction. P(A, B) = P(A) × P(B|A), which is at most P(A) whatever the dependence, so the "one strike and it's out" reading the essay offers next is exact. Correlation changes only how much the second conjunct is charged. In the Reagan example the correlation runs against the objection: federal support for unwed mothers was a liberal policy and cutting support to local governments a conservative one, so for Reagan the second is, if anything, less likely given the first. The essay's arithmetic undercharges rather than overcharges. Support theory is the formal home of the effect, and its explanation, that unpacked descriptions recruit more evidential support than packed ones, is the essay's "corroborative detail" in other words (Tversky & Koehler 1994).
